title: Catholic funerals
hookLine: vigil, funeral Mass, burial, with the white pall recalling baptism
tomorrow: Abuela still sets out two coffee cups. is that okay?

lines: A WHITE CLOTH OVER THE COFFIN.
cards: Anyone who has been to a Catholic funeral may have seen it. At the church doors, before the Mass begins, someone unfolds a big white cloth and lays it over the coffin.
It covers everything: polished wood or plain, whatever the person did or didn't get right. Why white, and why there at the door? The answer goes back to the very start of a Catholic life.

teach.b: The cloth is the pall, and it recalls the white garment a person is wrapped in at baptism. Paul ties the two together, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "For we are buried together with him by baptism into death."
So a funeral finishes what baptism began, and it comes in stages.
A vigil the night before, with prayers and often a rosary. The funeral Mass, where the coffin is sprinkled with holy water, another echo of the font, and the Easter candle burns beside it.

As the coffin leaves, an old chant asks the angels to lead the person into paradise. Then the last prayers at the grave. The Church permits cremation too, and asks that the ashes be buried or kept in a sacred place.
Here's one to tell a friend: Muslims have words for the moment death news arrives, from the Qur'an, in Pickthall's translation: "Lo! we are Allah's and lo! unto Him we are returning."
Catholics, in their own words, commend the one who died back to God.
The shared ground is real: at a death, both say the person belongs to God and goes back to God.
The honest difference: the pall speaks of baptism, a Christian sacrament Islam doesn't have, and Muslims pray their own funeral prayer, the janazah. Two ways of saying goodbye, ranking neither.

how: A Catholic funeral usually has three parts: a vigil or wake with prayers, a funeral Mass with the pall, holy water and the Easter candle, and the committal at the grave or place of burial.

games.why: the Qur'an says we are Allah's and unto Him we return; Catholics commend the dead back to God. the honest difference: the pall's baptism, and Islam's own janazah prayer.

practice: On a card or in your notes, write two funeral wishes: one reading or song, and one person you'd want to pray or speak. If you wrote a wish earlier this week, keep them together. Then let the sit be still around them.
